# @vllnt/analytics

> Cookie consent state and consent-gated event tracking for React and TypeScript, with Do Not Track and an SSR consent cookie.

Facts for AI tools. The library has no transport: it queues and gates events, and only
`console.log`s them when `debug: true`. Events never leave the page.

## For coding agents

The docs are bundled in the package at `node_modules/@vllnt/analytics/docs/`, with this file,
`CHANGELOG.md` and the TypeScript sources in `src/`. They match the installed version. Read them
before writing code.

## When to use

- Use it when a React app needs cookie-banner state stored in `localStorage` and a cookie.
- Use it when tracking calls must wait for consent and stop on Do Not Track or a decline.
- Use it when server code must read the visitor's choice from the `Cookie` header.
- Do not use it when events must reach a backend: it sends nothing; use your analytics vendor's SDK.
- Do not use it for a server-side consent record: use `@vllnt/convex-consent`.

## Package

- npm: `@vllnt/analytics` (MIT), repo: https://github.com/vllnt/analytics
- Unreleased builds from `main` use the `canary` dist-tag
- Ships ESM, CommonJS and type declarations from `dist` (built with tsup); both builds of
  `./react` start with `"use client"`
- Entry points: `@vllnt/analytics` (core + consent + types), `@vllnt/analytics/react` (`AnalyticsProvider`, `useAnalytics`, `useConsent`, `initAnalytics`)
- Peer dependency: React `^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0`
- Install: `pnpm add @vllnt/analytics`

## Behaviour

- Events tracked before `initAnalytics()` are queued and flushed on the first unblocked init;
  a blocked init drops them. The queue has no size limit.
- `initAnalytics()` blocks tracking when Do Not Track is on (`"1"` or `"yes"`) or stored consent
  has `analytics: false`. With no stored consent it starts tracking. `AnalyticsProvider` calls it
  while consent has `analytics: true` and calls `disableAnalytics()` after a stored decline, so a
  declined visitor's events are dropped. Before the user responds, events are queued in memory,
  except after `resetConsent()`, which blocks and drops events until the user responds again.
- Once blocked, only `enableAnalytics(config)` unblocks; it re-reads stored consent.
- Consent is stored in `localStorage` (`vllnt:analytics-consent`) and a `vllnt-consent` cookie
  (`1` or `0`) for SSR; `getConsentFromCookie(cookieString)` reads it with an anchored match.
- Consent is versioned; a stored version below the hook's `consentVersion` (default
  `CONSENT_VERSION`) re-prompts once, and the hooks save the new choice with that version.
- `track()` ignores empty or non-string names; `identify()` ignores empty or non-string ids.
- Browser APIs are guarded, so server-side import is safe. `initAnalytics()` has no server
  guard and starts the process-wide instance there, so call it only in the browser.
- The only thrown error is `useAnalytics must be used within an AnalyticsProvider`; there are no
  error codes.
